title: Turn It Off, Rotate Everything
subtitle: This week in Bitcoin & Nostr news

topics.title: Live Dashboard & Market
topics.description: Hot October inflation, a December hike priced in, the ETFs' worst week since June, Strategy buying again, and MSCI's verdict tonight

slides.heading: Live Dashboard
slides.body: Where Bitcoin sits right now. The full dashboards:

slides.heading: Market: Hot CPI, Cold Flows
slides.body: Inflation ran hot and the ETFs bled. The live price is on the dashboard.
bullets: October CPI +0.4%, core +0.3%, both above forecast. Markets now fully price a Fed hike on Dec 8–9
Spot ETFs Nov 2–6: −$1.28B, the worst week since late June. IBIT was ~$1.21B of it
Strategy +1,036 BTC, now 850,364, plus a $188M STRC buyback
Square takes Lightning at checkout: 0% until Dec 31, then 1%. $600 per payment cap
MSCI decides tonight, 5 PM ET, whether Strategy and Metaplanet stay in its indexes

topics.title: LNbits: Turn It Off, Rotate Everything
topics.description: After a wave of attacks, LNbits told every operator to shut down. 1.7.0 and 1.7.1 are out, but upgrading alone doesn't evict an attacker

slides.heading: LNbits: Turn It Off, Rotate Everything
slides.body: Sunday: "stop their LNbits servers IMMEDIATELY." Tuesday: 1.7.0. Today: 1.7.1. Every earlier version can lose funds.
bullets: Sun Nov 8: disable the Paywall extension, then stop all servers "following a wave of attacks." Hosted SaaS paused
Mon–Tue: SSRF and Nostr relay URL fixes land in dev, extensions auto-update. No release yet, keep it off
Tue Nov 10: 1.7.0, "funds running on prior versions of LNbits are at risk of being stolen"
Wed Nov 11: 1.7.1 rotates auth keys. The exploited bug isn't named yet; a report is promised

slides.heading: Upgrading Doesn't Evict a Guest
slides.body: An attacker who already took keys keeps them after the update. LNbits' checklist:
bullets: Suspect a compromise? Start from a fresh server
Super Admin → Settings → Users → Reset Wallet Keys
Revoke and replace funding-source API keys and macaroons. Rotate every other stored secret
Recreate NWC, LNDHub, Bolt Card, TPOS, Bleskomat and FOSSA connections
Who here runs LNbits for a meetup, a shop or the family?

topics.title: Who's Selling at the Bottom, and Why
topics.description: Miners, treasury companies and whales are moving coins 40% below the peak. Their own filings say why, and not all of it is bearish

slides.heading: Who's Selling at the Bottom, and Why
slides.body: Bitcoin sits ~41% under its $126K peak. Their own filings explain the selling.
bullets: Mining barely pays: Riot's Q3 all-in cost was $78,805 a coin, vs $70,855 earned. Hashprice ~$32/PH/day
AI pays more: Riot's 15-year, 910 MW AI lease is ~$1.8B a year. It sold 20,264 BTC this year to build
Debt: MARA sold 13,597 BTC (~40%) and repaid $750M of BTC-backed loans. Convertible puts come next year
Core Scientific and IREN leave mining by Dec 31. Bitdeer mined 3,855 BTC and kept 47

slides.heading: Not All Selling Is Bearish
bullets: Below NAV, buybacks win: Strategy sold 1,690 BTC at $64,262 in August to buy back STRC
Whales swap self-custody into IBIT, ~$3.6B in kind: safety, estate planning, usually no tax hit. Not cash sales
BlackRock's Mitchnick: "The current moment is the highest we've seen at any point"
"Bottom"? August's $64K was lower. And Strategy is buying again
For the room: forced sellers, or miners making a smart trade for AI power?

topics.title: Security Desk: Core Opens the Vault
topics.description: Bitcoin Core discloses three bugs it fixed a year ago, plus this week's patch pile: Electrum, Core Lightning, Bisq and Alby Hub

slides.heading: Security Desk: Core Opens the Vault
slides.body: Three advisories, all fixed in Core 30.0 (Oct 2025), published once 29.x hit end of life on Oct 27.
bullets: CVE-2025-62861 (high): a reorg wrongly evicts TRUC txs; a miner "can no longer create block templates" until restart
Hit 28.0–28.2 and 29.0–29.1. A miner problem, not consensus, not theft
CVE-2025-62860: Tor inbound peers got -whitelist on "thousands of reachable mainnet nodes"
CVE-2025-62859: a peer could stall block processing up to 10 minutes per try via compact blocks
This closes the W44 thread: the new disclosure policy, working as written

slides.heading: Patch Pile
slides.body: Update the wallet or node you actually use.
bullets: Electrum 4.8.4: malformed Lightning onion messages could drop your channel peer. Third security release in ~3 weeks
Liana 16.0: a rogue Electrum server could fake a broadcast so your fee bump paid the attacker. Fixed
Also patch: Core Lightning 26.06.10, Bisq 1.10.11 (required to trade), Alby Hub 1.24.6
Chainalysis got breached: user names, password hashes, live tokens. KYT back Nov 10 with forced resets
Still open: Citrine 3.2.2's notes don't mention the READ_EVENTS leak (CVE-2026-107045)

topics.title: Mining: Binance Pool Goes Dark
topics.description: Binance switched off its pool, difficulty heads for a big cut Friday, and PJM writes the rules for miners paid to switch off

slides.heading: Mining: Binance Pool Goes Dark
slides.body: Binance's pool, cloud mining and accelerator ended Nov 10, 2:00 AM EST. 22,213 blocks all-time, one in its last week.
bullets: ~26 EH/s in Dec 2025, 9.2 EH/s by October, under 1% of the network
Difficulty: about −7% at block 975,744, ~Friday. Blocks run ~10.8 minutes. Last one was +5.5%
PJM pays miners to curtail only if mining was profitable that hour. Nothing above 27 J/TH in 2026
Small miners: Stratum V2, OCEAN or solo? Two solo CKPool blocks landed seven hours apart Nov 7–8

topics.title: Bitcoin Dev: Testnet 5 Launches Friday
topics.description: Testnet 5's genesis block lands with mainnet's retarget, plus BIP54 odds, Knots' soft fork, quantum landmines and anti-exfil

slides.heading: Bitcoin Dev: Testnet 5 Launches Friday
slides.body: AJ Towns will mine testnet 5's genesis at mainnet block 975,744, the same block as Friday's retarget.
bullets: BIP95 genesis: pool-mineable, unspendable OP_RETURN output, default P2P port 18353
0%-fee solo pool for bootstrapping. A Bitaxe can help
Mining-software gotcha: heights 1–16 need OP_1–OP_16 for BIP34, not a one-byte push

slides.heading: Soft Fork Watch
bullets: Matt Corallo puts BIP54 (Great Consensus Cleanup) at ~80% odds of being next: timewarp, slow blocks, 64-byte txs
Knots 29.5 ships a coinbase-maturity soft fork from block 979,919. Non-DATUM pool miners: "expect no rewards"
Cory Fields' quantum landmines: hidden outputs that let owners claw coins back from a quantum thief. A thought experiment
Anti-exfil draft BIPs: the host adds to every nonce so a bad signer can't leak your seed
Blockstream runs a public signet with Simplicity on, plus the SimplicityHL toolchain

topics.title: Policy Corner: Rails Cut, Rails Granted
topics.description: FinCEN cuts MEXC off, the $250 Travel Rule plan dies, Coinbase gets a trust charter, Binance France closes, and Paraguay freezes a bank

slides.heading: Policy Corner: Rails Cut, Rails Granted
bullets: FinCEN cuts MEXC Global off from U.S. rails over $16B in alleged illicit flows, incl. Iran and North Korea
FinCEN and the Fed withdraw the 2020 plan to drop the Travel Rule threshold from $3,000 to $250
OCC grants Coinbase National Trust Company its final charter (Nov 6): custody, no deposits or lending
Russia: retail can buy BTC from Nov 17, capped at ₽300k a year. Moscow Exchange trading follows Dec 1

slides.heading: Self-Custody Lessons of the Week
bullets: Binance France closes every account Dec 31. From Nov 29, leftover balances pay 0.025% a month or 10 USDC
Leftovers after Dec 31 may be "converted, transferred or otherwise processed"
Paraguay seizes Ueno Bank: ~3 million customers, ~60% of adults, locked out
Deposit insurance covers ~US$38K, but the first payout is capped at ~US$1,700
Varoufakis's DiEM25 lost its Belgian bank account, donations stuck inside

links.label: Novara: DiEM25 loses its bank account
ABC Color: BCP on Ueno Bank

topics.title: Wallet Watch: Privacy by Default
topics.description: Bull Bitcoin makes every on-chain trade a Payjoin, SeedLock does silent payments with Sparrow, and two wallets get safer defaults

slides.heading: Wallet Watch: Privacy by Default
bullets: Bull Bitcoin: every on-chain buy or sell from BULL Wallet is a Payjoin by default. Chain analysis gets noisier
SeedLock 0.4.0: silent payments end to end with Sparrow 2.5+. One reusable sp1q… address, reproducible builds
JoinMarket-NG 0.43.0: Tor flood caps, fee-rate ceiling 100 sat/vB, confirm PSBT before broadcast
Bitcoin-Safe 2.3.0: scheduled payouts and wallet alerts over Nostr, Telegram or webhook

topics.title: Nostr This Week: Communities Grow Up
topics.description: Vector and Flotilla ship Discord-style communities, Nostur signs you into web apps without your key, and Marmot wins a hackathon

slides.heading: Nostr This Week: Communities Grow Up
bullets: Vector 0.5.0 "Vigil": Communities with roles, voice and video, Vector Web, Tor/I2P. Migrate Concord v1 first
Flotilla 1.15.0: thread boards, search, scheduled posts, on-device event store
Nostur 1.35.0 (iOS): sign in to Nostr web apps without sharing your key, plus NIP-88 polls
Zapstore 2.0.4 refuses an APK the listed key didn't sign

slides.heading: Specs and a Hackathon
bullets: btc++ Seoul: BlackIce won. Frostsnap signers co-sign silent payments over a Marmot group (hackathon code)
NIP-D9 (open PR): a no_delete tag so an event can't be retracted, for shared keys and coerced users
NIP-01 merged: relays can send a retry-after when you're rate-limited
NWC logout (PR #2537): an app can revoke its own wallet connection

topics.title: AI Corner: Agents With Wallets
topics.description: Block's Buzz hits 1.0, an agent wallet with spending limits, L402 by the token, and HRF money for AI you run yourself

slides.heading: AI Corner: Agents With Wallets
bullets: Block's Buzz 1.0: "a workspace where humans and agents build together, on a relay you own." Apache-2.0
bursar: a local daemon holds the key, the agent gets a token. Cashu, spending limits, Touch ID (unaudited)
Aperture 0.6.0: one Lightning payment buys tokens each request draws down. Sell LLM inference by the token
Wavelength's MCP server: one command and an agent can send and receive over Lightning

slides.heading: AI You Run Yourself
bullets: HRF funds six local, private AI projects, incl. an offline model for North Korea and antirez's DS4
Pawavox (Nigeria): election evidence signed on Nostr over 2G, plus a walled-off "ElectionGPT." Pilot: 142 reports
NIP draft #2536: kinds 4200/4201 for agents to bid, award and review work over Nostr
For the room: should an agent get its own npub, or act under yours?

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: Two Ecash Cards
topics.description: Fedimint Card and Cashu Card: tap-to-pay ecash on the same blank smart card, both built by Island Bitcoin and Dread, and now both fit on one card

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: Two Ecash Cards
slides.body: Same blank NXP J3R180 smart card, two ecash systems, one builder team. Tap to pay, even offline.
bullets: Fedimint Card: the card holds each note's spend key and signs. No change to Fedimint, works with existing federations
Cashu Card: last week's Spotlight, one week on. Offline sales now settle end to end
Nov 9 bench test: both applets side by side on one J3R180, in either install order
Built by Island Bitcoin (freedom tech for the Caribbean) and Dread. MIT, both experimental

slides.heading: Fedimint Card: Live in a Federation
bullets: In production for the Island Bitcoin Community federation since Nov 6, on 32-slot cards
The kit: a till on StartOS, a Setup app for operators, POS apps for Android and iOS (beta builds Nov 8)
Applet 3.0 takes offline charges. Since Nov 10 the POS phone takes the tap when the till is unreachable
Top up over Lightning at the POS. Optional daily limit per card, for a village batch
Their warning: "Put on a card only what you can afford to lose"

slides.heading: Cashu Card: Week Two
bullets: Applet 2.2: an offline till charged 7 sats, the card carried the record, a later tap settled it with the mint
The till got its 7 sats back exactly once. Tested Nov 6 with a Pixel, an iPhone and a live mint
Provisioner build 15 (Nov 10): finds mints over Nostr (NIP-87) with their reviews
A second card model, the J3R452, now provisions like the J3R180
Back it at cashucard.org/fund: Lightning, on-chain, Cashu or Fedimint ecash

topics.title: Quick Tip: Updating Isn't Revoking
topics.description: LNbits' lesson for every wallet and node: a patch closes the door, but it doesn't take back the keys someone already copied

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Updating Isn't Revoking
slides.body: A patch closes the hole. It doesn't cancel keys someone already copied.
bullets: An NWC string, a macaroon, an API key: each one is a spending key. Treat them like seeds
List every connection your wallet or node has handed out. Delete the ones you don't use
After any incident: update, then rotate. New keys, new connections
Keep a hot wallet small. Everything else lives on keys you hold offline
